works.title: Five Piano Pieces (The Soldier, Fiery Sonata, The Noise of a Train, The Storm, The Tempest)
works.notes: Lost. Shostakovich used a theme from this work in "Immortality" from the Suite on Verses of Michelangelo Buonarroti.

works.title: Hymn to Freedom
works.notes: Lost

works.title: Funeral March in Memory of the Victims of the Revolution
works.notes: Originally assigned Op. 5 along with Nostalgia. Dedicated to the memories of Kadets Fyodor Kokoshkin and Andrei Shingaryov, who were murdered on January 20, 1918, at the Mariinskaya Hospital.

works.title: Nostalgia
works.notes: Originally assigned Op. 5 along with Funeral March in Memory of the Victims of the Revolution. Alternately known as Melancholia and The Soldier Reminiscing About his Homeland, which is unrelated to "The Soldier" from the Five Piano Pieces.

works.title: Piano Pieces from the Exercise Book "1919" (Piece in C major, Prelude-March, In the Forest)
Variations on Mikhail Glinka's "The Lark"
works.notes: Unfinished

works.title: Bagatelle
works.notes: Dedicated to Marianna Fyodorovna Gramenitskaya.

works.title: Two Preludes
works.notes: Originally assigned Op. 1. Second piece is a revised version of the Bagatelle; dedicated to Boris Kustodiev.

works.title: Exercise Pieces
works.notes: Consists of six pieces, the fifth of which is based on "In the Forest".

works.title: Three Pieces (Minuet, Prelude, and Intermezzo)
works.notes: Last piece incomplete. Extant manuscript, which was not written in Shostakovich's hand, was preserved by Alexandra Rozanova, who had been his piano teacher 1917–spring 1919.

works.title: Piano Sonata in B minor
works.notes: Incomplete. Third movement orchestrated and assigned Op. 1. Part of the slow movement was orchestrated for an early attempt at a symphony, then later incorporated into the Piano Trio No. 1.

works.title: Eight Preludes
works.notes: Manuscript was destroyed by Shostakovich, but copies survived.

works.title: Five Preludes
works.notes: Selected by Shostakovich from the Eight Preludes as his contribution to an incomplete collaborative cycle of 24 preludes in all keys composed with fellow students Grigori Klements and Pavel Feldt.

works.title: Three Pieces (Humoreske, Fugicha, Chromatic Fugue)
works.notes: Partially lost

works.title: Three Fantastic Dances
works.notes: Originally published as Op. 1. Shostakovich orchestrated the first dance for a class exercise (unpublished).

works.title: Seven Fugues
works.notes: The fifth fugue quotes the second Kyrie eleison from Bach's Mass in B minor.

works.title: Dance
works.notes: Dedicated to Zoya Shostakovich; work later reused in the score to Alone.

works.title: Piano Sonata
works.notes: Lost. Two letters by Shostakovich and an entry in Steinberg's diary attest to its existence.

works.title: Piano Sonata No. 1
works.notes: Originally named October or October Sonata.

works.title: Aphorisms
works.notes: Its ten pieces were selected from an original set of twelve.

works.title: Four Fugues (C major, A minor, G major, E minor)
works.notes: The second fugue was reused with little alteration in Op. 87.

works.title: Piano Sonata No. 2 in B minor
Children's Notebook
works.notes: Composed for Galina Shostakovich. The fanfare that initiates "Birthday" was reused in the Festive Overture, while "Clockwork Doll" reuses a theme from Op. 1.

works.title: Murzilka
works.notes: Probably composed by Shostakovich for his children around the time of the Children's Notebook.

works.title: Eleven Variations on a Theme by Mikhail Glinka
works.notes: Based on a theme from A Life for the Tsar. Collaborative project with Eugen Kapp, Vissarion Shebalin, Andrei Eshpai, Rodion Shchedrin, Georgi Sviridov, Yuri Levitin, and Dmitry Kabalevsky to commemorate the centennial of Glinka's death. Shostakovich contributed variations VIII, IX, and XI.
